claims.text: The starting material is a heterogeneous, multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy that has not undergone dynamic amorphization or surface refinement.
Concurrent elevated-temperature wear and corrosion induce dynamic amorphization in the alloy's near-surface region.
Mechanical wear produces an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The transformed surface layer has increased grain-boundary density and high grain-boundary energy.
The newly generated grain boundaries are reactive sites that accelerate corrosion at elevated temperature.
High-energy grain boundaries act as preferential sites for oxide formation or localized corrosion.
Corrosion damage softens or otherwise compromises the transformed surface.
Corrosion-induced loss of surface integrity makes the alloy more vulnerable to wear.
Wear-induced microstructural refinement and corrosion-induced mechanical weakening form a positive degradation feedback loop.
Total degradation under simultaneous wear and corrosion is greater than under isolated wear or isolated corrosion at comparable elevated temperature.
Simultaneous exposure causes a significant increase in corrosion rate because of the additional reactive grain-boundary sites.
Simultaneous exposure causes a moderate increase in wear because corrosion compromises structural integrity.
The coupled acceleration requires a temperature high enough to promote oxidation and dynamic microstructural transformation.
The coupled acceleration may be absent in inert environments where oxidation is limited.
The coupled acceleration may be absent at low temperature.
A surface-stabilized group that inhibits dynamic amorphization should exhibit less coupled degradation than an untreated group under identical exposure.
The untreated group should develop a statistically significant increase in near-surface grain-boundary density.

contradictions.description: The same near-surface layer is described as dynamically amorphized and ultra-nanocrystalline with abundant grain boundaries. A fully amorphous layer lacks crystalline grains and grain boundaries; a transient, mixed, or partially amorphous structure would need to be specified to reconcile these descriptions.
